mentl/6dcb9a9:
PLAN.md was 10,809 lines, 7,002 of them a hand-written prose copy of 448
commits and 1,474 a peer catalog. That is the Carried-Truth Law violated
at the doc layer, and section 7's own destiny sentence had said so for
months. The landing record moves to LEDGER.md and the named peers to
RESIDUE.md, both reference-only, consulted and never read whole. Nothing
was deleted or edited: 267 ledger entries in, 267 out, 107 peers
preserved. Read path 13,464 -> 4,366 lines.

PLAN keeps what is true and gains section 11, the ordered program that
replaces the five-column production bar. It is ordered by foundational
depth rather than symptom urgency, because performance falls out of the
design being right: a change justified by a number and not a law is the
wrong change. Total monomorphization is the erasure boundary lying, the
arena is ownership having a real reclaim, name-is-handle is a name being
an edge. Speed is the side effect in all three, and calling it the goal
is how a wrong change gets justified.

march.sh captures every gate it owns at repin and stamps a red board;
a gate that was not run is now a visible blank instead of an omission.
The crown went unreported for eleven consecutive entries while a
higher-order effect leak rode the arc, and nothing written was false --
the gate had merely stopped being mentioned.

doc-truth refuses that marker, and gains the verb namespace: the tools/
sweep existed from birth while mentl <verb> was never checked, so the
docs could promise a verb the CLI does not serve. The verb list is read
from mentl help so no second roster can drift. It also reads the head pin
from LEDGER.md, where an empty result now fails rather than passing
silently -- without that, the move would have turned the pin chain into a
gate that cannot fail.

SYNTAX gains a one-home list of the verbs it declares ahead of the CLI.
The authority may lead the lathe; that licence is also how a promise rots
unnoticed, so the lag is a checked list that shrinks as verbs lan

sonido/6d8ed48:
LL(1) recursive descent parser that compiles a text spec into a
ProcessingGraph DAG. Supports linear chains (`a | b | c`), parallel
splits with 2-16 paths (`split(a; b)`), dry pass-through (`-`), nested
splits, and per-effect parameters (`delay:time=300,feedback=0.4`).

Two-phase design: parse → GraphSpec (pure IR, testable) → build →
ProcessingGraph (audio-ready). New `--graph` flag on `sonido process`
conflicts with `--effect`/`--chain`/`--preset`. Output filenames encode
topology slugs for traceability.

28 unit tests covering parser, validation, graph construction, slug
generation, and audio round-trip. 7 graph topology demo scripts added.
sonido/6d9362b:
Add fast_math module with six approximation functions targeting
Cortex-M7 where libm transcendentals dominate CPU budgets:

- fast_log2: IEEE 754 decomposition + minimax polynomial (<0.2%)
- fast_exp2: floor/frac split + 3rd-order polynomial (<0.2%)
- fast_db_to_linear / fast_linear_to_db: compose above (<0.05 dB)
- fast_sin_turns: Bhaskara-corrected parabola (<0.001 abs)
- fast_tan: Padé [2/1] rational approximation (<0.1% for f<sr/4)

These are the foundation for CM7 budget optimizations identified by
the swarm audit — all four over-budget effects (ParametricEq,
MultiVibrato, Compressor, Phaser) are dominated by libm calls that
these functions replace at 10-20× lower cycle cost.
